hindi: इस प्रकार स्थित रहते हुए दोष शरीर पर अनुग्रह करते हैं यानी उसे सहारा देते हैं।
english: The doṣas, remaining thus, favour (support) the body.
notes: 'evam' (thus) points back to a statement outside this unit; the state of the doṣas is not described here. 'sthitāḥ hi' is written sthitā hi by regular sandhi. anugṛhṇanti = favour, help, sustain; 'support' is the plain sense.

hindi: किन्तु व्यत्यय यानी उलट से पीड़ा देते हैं।
english: But by reversal (vyatyaya) they afflict.
notes: Elliptical: the subject (the doṣas of 42) is carried over and not supplied; no object is stated. vyatyaya = reversal, inversion, the contrary (of the state in 42).

hindi: वहाँ श्याव यानी साँवली-भूरी और अरुण यानी लाल, फड़कने वाली, सूक्ष्म, क्षण में भरी और क्षण में खाली, वात-रक्त को वहन करती हैं।
english: There, the dusky-brown and reddish, throbbing, fine (ones), momentarily full and momentarily empty, carry Vāta-blood (vāta-rakta).
notes: The adjectives are feminine plural and stand for an unstated feminine noun (dhamanī or sirā are both feminine); the noun is not given here, so none is supplied. 'riktā vāta-' is regular sandhi (riktāḥ + vāta-). vāta-rakta is read here as 'blood of the Vāta type' (the series 44-48 classifies blood by doṣa, ending with 'pure blood'); it is probably not the disease vātarakta (probable, not certain). śyāva = dusky/dark brown, aruṇa = reddish.

hindi: नीली, पीली और काली, स्पर्श में उष्ण, शीघ्र स्रवित होने वाली: पित्त-रक्त।
english: Blue, yellow and dark (ones), warm to the touch, quickly discharging: Pitta-blood (pitta-rakta).
notes: Elliptical: the verb vahanti (carry) is carried from 44 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. The three colours are read as a dvandva (blue, yellow and dark); asita = dark/black. srāvin = discharging, oozing (what is discharged is not stated).

hindi: गोरी, स्निग्ध यानी चिकनी, स्थिर, ठण्डी, खुजली वाली: कफ-रक्त।
english: Fair, unctuous, steady, cold, itching (ones): Kapha-blood (kapha-rakta).
notes: Elliptical: the verb vahanti (carry) is carried from 44 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. gaurī = fair, whitish-yellow (the plain sense 'fair' is kept). kaṇḍūmatī = having itching (kaṇḍū); whose itching is not stated.

hindi: लक्षणों के मिश्रण में: संसर्ग यानी मेल और सन्निपात यानी संयोग का रक्त।
english: In a mixture of the signs: blood of saṃsarga (combination) and sannipāta (union).
notes: Elliptical: the verb vahanti (carry) is carried from 44 and is not supplied. The compound saṃsarga-sannipāta-rakta is read as 'blood of saṃsarga and of sannipāta' (a dvandva joined to rakta); saṃsarga and sannipāta are the usual terms for combination of two doṣas and of all three, but the line itself does not count the doṣas, so the translation keeps the plain sense.

hindi: समान, गूढ़, स्निग्ध यानी चिकनी, रोहिणी यानी ऊपर चढ़ने वाली जिसका यहाँ अर्थ अनिश्चित है: शुद्ध रक्त।
english: Even, hidden, unctuous, rohiṇī (literally 'rising'; sense here uncertain) (ones): pure blood (śuddha-rakta).
notes: Elliptical: the verb vahanti (carry) is carried from 44 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. The print joins two words (samāgūḍhāḥ = samāḥ gūḍhāḥ by regular sandhi, a spacing slip; no flag); 'snigdhā rohiṇyaḥ' is likewise snigdhāḥ rohiṇyaḥ. rohiṇī is not enriched: it can mean rising/growing (or red); the sense in this list is uncertain. The closing 'iti' ends the five-fold list of 44-48 and is not translated.

words.gloss: dhamanīs (vessels, channels; probably blood vessels, probable)

hindi: धमनियाँ यानी सम्भवतः रक्तवाहिकाएँ तो चौबीस हैं।
english: The dhamanīs (vessels, probably blood vessels), however, are twenty-four.
notes: Copula understood. dhamanī = vessel or channel; the reading 'blood vessel' is probable, and whether artery is meant specifically is disputed. The count twenty-four is translated as printed (it agrees with the 10 + 10 + 4 of unit 53).

hindi: इनसे यह शरीर, जल ले जाने वालियों से उद्यान की तरह और कुल्याओं यानी नहरों से खेत की तरह, आर्द्र होता है।
english: By these, this body is moistened, like a garden by water-carrying (ones) and like a field by canals (kulyā).
notes: 'tābhiḥ' (by them) refers back to the dhamanīs of 49. 'jalahāriṇībhiḥ' is feminine and qualifies an unstated noun, shown as '(ones)'. 'ārāmaḥ iva' is written ārāma iva by regular sandhi; the avagraha in kāyo'yam is the usual ayam after -o. upasnihyati is an active form, 'becomes moist'; 'is moistened' is the natural English with an agent.

hindi: और इनसे नाभि घिरी हुई है, अनुमानित पाठ पर चक्र की नाभि के अरों से घिरे होने के समान।
english: And by these the navel is surrounded, on a conjectural reading like the hub of a wheel by its spokes.

text_flags.why: possible: 'āraikariva' is not a word; 'arair iva' (like by spokes) fits the wheel-hub simile and the sense of 'āvṛtā'; the extra 'ka' and the long ā look like print slips

notes: The printed string 'āraikariva' cannot be parsed as it stands; 'arair iva' (like by spokes) is a conjectural restoration that suits the wheel-hub simile and the following 'āvṛtā' (the extra 'ka' looks like a print slip). Marked conjectural in both translations. 'cakranābhi' is taken as the hub of a wheel; 'āvṛtā' agrees with nābhiḥ (feminine). Copula understood.

hindi: इस कारण नाभि में विशेष रूप से प्राण स्थित हैं; और क्योंकि वह, अनुमानित पाठ पर, भीतर भी अधिष्ठान यानी आधार है।
english: Therefore the prāṇas (vital breaths) are established especially in the navel; and since it, on a conjectural reading, is also within a seat (adhiṣṭhāna)

text_flags.why: possible: 'sāṃ' with ṃ is unexplained; sā antar api adhiṣṭhānam ('it also within is a seat') gives a construable reading; the anusvara looks like a print slip

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue in 53; the 'yataḥ' clause has no main clause in this unit, so the English is left open. The last token 'sāṃ'tarapyadhiṣṭhānaṃ' is read as sā antar api adhiṣṭhānam (the printed ṃ before the avagraha looks like a slip); 'sā' is taken to be the navel (feminine), which is a conjecture, hence conjectural marks and low confidence. 'viśeṣeṇaprāṇā' = viśeṣeṇa prāṇāḥ (spacing slip). prāṇa: kept as 'prāṇa (vital breath)'; no modern equivalent forced.

hindi: उन धमनियों में निश्चय ही, अनुमानित पाठ पर, दस ऊपर की ओर फैली हैं, दस नीचे की ओर और चार तिरछी।
english: Of those dhamanīs indeed, on a conjectural reading, ten have spread upward, ten downward, four crosswise.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ddha' for 'da' and 'au' for 'o' are typical print errors; daśa ūrdhvam ('ten upward') parallels 'daśādhaḥ' (ten downward) and 'catasras tiryak' and gives the total of 24
possible: pra-mṛta means 'dead' and does not fit; pra-sṛta 'spread out' fits vessels, and sa/ma are confusable in this print

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 52. Two print damages, both conjectural: 'ddhaśaurdhvaṃ' read as daśa ūrdhvam (dd/d and au/o confusions) and 'pramṛtā' read as prasṛtāḥ (pra-mṛta would mean 'dead'; sa/ma confusion). The reading is supported by the total: ten + ten + four = twenty-four, the number given in 49. The nouns for 'ten', 'four' are the dhamanīs; the numerals are translated as printed.

hindi: तब उनसे अपने-अपने अनुसार अंग और अवयव धारण किए जाते हैं और पुष्ट किए जाते हैं।
english: Then, by them, the limbs and their parts, each according to its own, are held and nourished.
notes: 'tataḥ' (then, thence) is kept in its plain sense; it may also be read as 'therefore'. 'avayavāḥ dhāryante' is written avayavā dhāryante by regular sandhi. 'aṅgāvayavāḥ' is read as 'limbs and parts', each limb with its parts.

hindi: इनमें से ऊपर जाने वाली हृदय तक पहुँचकर प्रत्येक तीन प्रकार की हो जाती हैं।
english: Of these, the upward-going (ones), having reached the heart (hṛdaya), each come to be threefold.
notes: The three kinds are not named in this unit (the next unit counts thirty). 'ūrdhvagāḥ hṛdayam' is written ūrdhvagā hṛdayam by regular sandhi.

words.gloss: Vāta; Pitta; Kapha; blood (rakta); rasa (the nutrient fluid, first dhātu; standard)
carrying (on a possible correction; printed vahantaḥ)

hindi: फिर तीस के बीच दो-दो वात, पित्त, कफ, रक्त और रस यानी पोषक द्रव को वहन करने वाली।
english: Then, among the thirty, two and two, carrying Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, blood (rakta) and rasa (the nutrient fluid).

text_flags.why: possible: 'dve dve' is feminine, so the participle should be feminine (vahantyaḥ); printed masculine vahantaḥ looks like a slip

notes: GROUPING: appears to begin a list that continues through 57-59 (the thirty are 10 + 8 + 8 + 4). There is no finite verb, only the participle; 'dve dve' is read as 'two each' over the five items. The printed 'vahantaḥ' is masculine plural and does not agree with the feminine 'dve dve' (expected vahantyaḥ); flagged as possible. 'vāta, pitta, kapha' are the doṣas; 'rasa' here is the nutrient fluid (dhātu), not taste.

hindi: आठ से शब्द, रूप, रस यानी स्वाद और गन्ध ग्रहण किए जाते हैं।
english: By eight, sound, form, taste and smell are grasped (perceived).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 56. Only four of the sense-objects are listed (touch is not named in this line). 'rūpa' = form (visible appearance); 'rasa' here is taste. 'gandhāḥ gṛhyante' is written gandhā gṛhyante by regular sandhi.

hindi: दो-दो से बोलता है, घोष यानी ध्वनि करता है, सोता है और जागता है।
english: By two and two, one speaks, makes a sound (ghoṣa), sleeps and wakes.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 56-57. The repeated 'dvābhyām' is read as distributive (two for each of the four acts, which gives eight). The text does not say which pair serves which act; the subject of the verbs is unstated. ghoṣa = sound, cry; its exact sense beside 'speaks' is not fixed.

hindi: दो आँसू वहन करती हैं; और स्तनों पर आश्रित दो: नारी का स्तन्य यानी दूध, नर का शुक्र यानी वीर्य नामक प्रजनन-द्रव।
english: Two carry tears; and two, resting on the breasts: a woman's milk (stanya), a man's semen (śukra).
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete the list of 56-58 (two for tears and two on the breasts make the last four of the thirty). Elliptical: for the second pair the verb vahataḥ (carry) is carried over and not supplied. 'nāryāḥ stanyam' is the printed joined form (nāryāḥstanyaṃ), a spacing slip.

hindi: नीचे जाने वाली, पक्वाशय यानी सम्भवतः बड़ी आँत के क्षेत्र में स्थित, इसी प्रकार तीन प्रकार की हो जाती हैं।
english: The downward-going (ones), situated in the pakvāśaya (the seat of digested matter, probably the large intestine region), likewise come to be threefold.
notes: The 'ones' are presumably the ten downward dhamanīs of 53, but the line itself does not name them. pakvāśaya = seat of the digested/ripened (food, stool): probably the colon/large-intestine region (probable). 'pakvāśayasthāḥ evam' is written pakvāśayasthā evam by regular sandhi.

hindi: वहाँ पहली दस: पहले के समान।
english: There, the first ten: as before.
notes: Elliptical and unclear: 'daśādyāḥ' is read as daśa ādyāḥ, 'the first ten', presumably of the thirty that arise from the downward group (60), and 'pūrvavat' as 'as before' (as in the upward group); neither referent is stated, so no verb or noun is supplied. 'daśādyāḥ' could also mean 'ten and so on'.

hindi: दो अन्न वहन करती हैं, आँतों के आश्रय से; दो जल, दो मूत्र; दो शुक्र यानी वीर्य नामक प्रजनन-द्रव वहन करती हैं; और दो छोड़ती हैं।
english: Two carry food, with the intestines (antra) as their resting-place; two, water; two, urine; two carry semen (śukra); and two release.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 60-61. For the 2nd, 3rd pairs the verb vahataḥ is carried over and not supplied. 'vahataḥ annam' is written vahato 'nnam by regular sandhi. The object of 'muñcataḥ' is not stated and is not supplied. 'antrāśrayeṇa' (instrumental) is read as 'having the intestines as resting-place'; it may qualify the food-carrying pair only.

hindi: वे ही दोनों: नारियों का आर्तव यानी रजोरक्त।
english: Those very two: of women, ārtava (menstrual blood).
notes: Elliptical: the verb (carry) is carried from 62 and is not supplied. 'te' probably refers to the pair that carries śukra in 62 (the parallel with 59), but the line does not say so.

words.gloss: thick, large; intestine; bound to, connected with

hindi: दो मल को बाहर निकालने वाली, अनुमानित पाठ पर, स्थूल आँत से बँधी; शेष आठ तिरछी जाने वाली स्वेद को तृप्त करती हैं।
english: Two that expel stool (varcas, on a conjectural reading), bound to the large intestine (sthūlāntra); but the remaining eight, running crosswise, nourish the sweat (sveda).

text_flags.why: possible: vajra ('thunderbolt') gives no sense here; varcas (stool) + nirasanī (expelling) with 'sthūlāntrapratibaddhe' fits the group of passages in 62; jr/rc is a plausible misreading

notes: The printed 'vajrronirasanyau' is read as varcas-nirasanyau ('expelling stool'): vajra (thunderbolt) gives no sense, and a stool-expelling pair bound to the large intestine fits the list of 62; conjectural, flagged. Hindi 'तृप्त करती हैं' keeps the literal 'satiate'; 'nourish' is the English sense (abhitarpayanti). The 'remaining eight' presumably complete a count not given in this line.

words.gram: pres. pass. part. √bhid, f. nom. pl.

words.gloss: become (on a possible correction; printed bhavati)

hindi: तिरछी जाने वाली चार विभक्त होती हुई बहुत प्रकार की हो जाती हैं, यह पहले कहा जा चुका है।
english: The four that go crosswise, being divided, become very manifold (in very many ways); this was stated before.

text_flags.why: possible: the subject 'catasraḥ ... bhidyamānāḥ' is plural, so the verb should be bhavanti; the singular looks like a print slip

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 64. The back-reference is probably to the 'four crosswise' of 53, though 'prāk' could point to an earlier chapter. The printed 'bhavati' is singular beside a plural subject; read as bhavanti, flagged as possible. 'iti uktam' is taken as 'this has been said'.

words.gloss: blood; path, passage (probably the passage of the menstrual blood)

hindi: पुरुषों के स्रोतस यानी शरीर के मार्ग नौ हैं: दो कान, दो नेत्र, दो नासापुट, मुख, पायु यानी गुदा और मूत्रमार्ग; और तीन अन्य स्त्रियों के: दोनों स्तन और रक्तपथ यानी सम्भवतः रजोरक्त का मार्ग।
english: The srotas (bodily channels, openings) of men are nine: the two ears, two eyes, two nostrils, mouth, anus (pāyu) and urinary passage; and three other (ones) of women: the two breasts and the blood-passage (rakta-patha, probably the passage of the menstrual blood).
notes: Copula understood. The nine are counted as listed: 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1. 'anyāni trīṇi' (three others) are then the women's: two breasts and the blood-passage. rakta-patha is not explained in the line; 'passage of the menstrual blood' is probable, not certain. pāyu = anus (standard). srotas is kept as a doctrinal term (channel).

words.gloss: prāṇa (vital breath); water; food; dhātu; mala

hindi: तथा अन्य भीतरी स्रोतस: जीवन के आयतन यानी आश्रय, तेरह; प्राण, जल, अन्न, धातु और मल के आयतन।
english: And the other inner srotas (channels): seats (āyatana) of life, thirteen; seats of prāṇa (vital breath), water, food, the dhātus and the malas.
notes: The avagraha in tathā'parāṇi is the print habit (ā + a gives ā). Copula understood. 'trayodaśa' (thirteen) is translated as printed; the line does not list the thirteen (the units 68-82 name some). The two predicates ('seats of life' and 'seats of prāṇa, water, food, dhātus and malas') are read as describing the same srotas. dhātu and mala are doctrinal terms and are kept without a modern equivalent.

hindi: वहाँ प्राण को वहन करने वालों का मूल हृदय और महास्रोतस है।
english: There, of the prāṇa-carrying (ones), the root (mūla) is the heart (hṛdaya) and the great channel (mahāsrotas).
notes: The 'prāṇa-carrying (ones)' are the prāṇavaha srotas of 67, left as an unstated noun. mahāsrotas is kept literally ('great channel'); its identification is disputed and is not given in the line.

words.gloss: exertion (the word continues in the next token)
urge; holding back; and the rest

hindi: वे क्षय, रूक्षता, प्यास, भूख, व्यायाम, वेगों को रोकने आदि से दूषित होते हैं।
english: They become vitiated by wasting (kṣaya), dryness (raukṣya), thirst, hunger, exertion (vyāyāma), holding back of urges (vega-dhāraṇa) and the like.
notes: The print breaks the word vyāyāma across two tokens (vyāyā | mavega-): a spacing slip, no flag; the 'ma' is read with the first word. 'tāni' refers to the prāṇa-carrying srotas of 68. kṣaya = wasting, loss (not the disease name, in this list of causes). vega-dhāraṇa = holding back natural urges.

hindi: तब उच्छ्वसन यानी साँस: अतिसृष्ट यानी अधिक छूटती हुई, रुकी हुई, कुपित, थोड़ी-थोड़ी या बार-बार, शब्द और पीड़ा सहित।
english: Then breathing (ucchvasana): excessively released, obstructed, agitated, scanty or frequent, with sound and pain.
notes: No finite verb; the adjectives are neuter and agree with ucchvasanam. The single 'vā' follows the last pair, so 'scanty or frequent' is the natural grouping; whether 'or' also runs through the earlier terms is not settled by the wording. 'saśabdaśūla' is read as 'with sound and pain'; it could also be 'with noisy pain'. 'alpālpam' = alpa-alpam, 'little by little, scanty'.

words.gloss: like śvāsa (breathlessness; dyspnoea or asthma-type, probable)

hindi: वहाँ साधन यानी चिकित्सा श्वास यानी साँस फूलने की बीमारी के समान, सम्भवतः दमा।
english: There, the treatment (sādhana) is as in śvāsa (breathlessness; probably dyspnoea of the asthma type).
notes: Copula understood. śvāsa = laboured breathing; reading it as the breathlessness disorder (asthma/dyspnoea type) is probable. The text refers to the treatment given elsewhere for śvāsa; it is not repeated here. 'sādhana' = means of accomplishing, treatment.

hindi: जल को वहन करने वालों का मूल तालु और क्लोम है, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है।
english: Of the water-carrying (ones), the root is the palate (tālu) and the kloma (identity disputed).
notes: kloma (kloman) is not identified in the line; the pancreas, the right lung and the trachea/throat have each been proposed (disputed), so it is kept as 'kloma'. 'kloma ca' is printed run together (klomaca). The unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'.

words.gloss: āma (undigested; sense uncertain here); fear; excessive drinking; heat; dry; food; holding back of thirst (on a conjectural reading); and the rest

hindi: वे आम यानी अपक्व या कच्चा जिसका यहाँ अर्थ अनिश्चित है, भय, अतिपान, उष्ण, सूखा अन्न, अनुमानित पाठ पर तृष्णा के निग्रह यानी रोकने आदि से दूषित होते हैं। तब अत्यधिक प्यास, मुख का सूखना, कानों में भनभनाहट और अँधेरा दिखना।
english: They become vitiated by āma (sense uncertain here), fear, excessive drinking, heat, dry food, holding back of thirst (on a conjectural reading) and the like. Then excessive thirst, dryness of the mouth, ringing (kṣveḍana, probably tinnitus-type) in the ears and seeing of darkness.

text_flags.why: possible: 'tṛṣṇi-' is not a stem; tṛṣṇā-nigraha ('holding back of thirst') is a natural cause for the water channels, and the dropped 'ān' is a plausible print slip

notes: 'tāni' refers to the water-carrying srotas of 72. 'āma' is kept unexplained (undigested matter or 'raw' are possible; the sense here is uncertain). The printed 'tṛṣṇigraha' is not a regular compound; read as tṛṣṇā-nigraha (holding back of thirst), a conjecture (flagged). 'atipāna' = excessive drinking (of what is not stated). kṣveḍana = humming/ringing sound; the tinnitus-type sense is probable. The list of signs has no verb.

hindi: वहाँ तृष्णा में कही गई औषध।
english: There, the medicine (auṣadha) stated for thirst (tṛṣṇā).
notes: Elliptical: no verb; 'the medicine said for thirst' refers to the treatment given elsewhere, which is not repeated here. tṛṣṇā = thirst.

words.gloss: āmāśaya (seat of undigested food; probably the stomach)

hindi: अन्न को वहन करने वालों का मूल आमाशय यानी सम्भवतः पेट है, और बायाँ पार्श्व।
english: Of the food-carrying (ones), the root is the āmāśaya (seat of undigested food, probably the stomach) and the left side (vāma-pārśva).
notes: The unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. āmāśaya = seat of āma (the unprocessed food): probably the stomach (probable). 'vāma-pārśva' = the left side (flank); not further specified.

words.gloss: Mātrāśitīya (name of a chapter, literally on the measure of what is eaten); said, stated

hindi: उनके दूषित होने पर सब कुछ मात्राशितीय में कहा हुआ जानना चाहिए।
english: In their vitiation, one should understand all as stated in the Mātrāśitīya.
notes: 'Mātrāśitīya' is taken as the name of a chapter (probably an earlier chapter of this work); the line does not say which, and it is not checked here. 'duṣṭau' = in vitiation (locative of duṣṭi).

hindi: रस को वहन करने वालों का मूल हृदय और दस धमनियाँ हैं।
english: Of the rasa-carrying (ones), the root is the heart (hṛdaya) and the ten dhamanīs (vessels).
notes: The unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. The ten dhamanīs are probably those of 53 and 55 (the upward ten that reach the heart), but the line does not say so. 'rasa' is the nutrient fluid (dhātu).

hindi: रक्त को वहन करने वालों के यकृत और प्लीहा।
english: Of the blood-carrying (ones): the liver (yakṛt) and the spleen (plīhan).
notes: Elliptical: 'mūlam' (root) is carried over from 77 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. 'yakṛt plīhā' are two words (yakṛt, plīhan nominative).

hindi: मांस को वहन करने वालों के स्नाव यानी सम्भवतः स्नायु या कण्डरा और त्वचा।
english: Of the flesh-carrying (ones): the sinews (snāva, probably tendons or ligaments) and the skin (tvac).
notes: Elliptical: 'mūlam' is carried over from 77 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. snāva (n.) is the print's form for sinew; probably the same as snāyu (probable).

hindi: मेद यानी वसा को वहन करने वालों के दोनों वृक्क यानी गुर्दे और मांस।
english: Of the fat-carrying (ones) (medas): the two kidneys (vṛkka) and the flesh (māṃsa).
notes: Elliptical: 'mūlam' is carried over from 77 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. 'medovāhinām vṛkkau' is printed run together (medovāhināṃvṛkkau), a spacing slip. medas = fat (standard).

hindi: अस्थि को वहन करने वालों के जघन यानी कूल्हा और मेद।
english: Of the bone-carrying (ones): the jaghana (hips or loins region, probable) and fat (medas).
notes: Elliptical: 'mūlam' is carried over from 77 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. jaghana is the hip or loin region, which part exactly is not stated (probable).

hindi: मज्जा को वहन करने वालों के पर्व यानी जोड़ और अस्थियाँ।
english: Of the marrow-carrying (ones): the joints (parvan) and the bones (asthi).
notes: Elliptical: 'mūlam' is carried over from 77 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(ones)'. The unit ends the list printed here; the later dhātu (śukra) and mala carriers are not in this chunk.
